title: Plate tectonics
statement: Plate tectonics models Earth's outer rigid shell as moving plates whose interactions help explain seafloor spreading, mountain building, earthquakes, volcanism, and the geographic distribution of many rocks and fossils.
limitations: The model does not make exact short-term earthquake predictions, and local geology remains important.

title: Water cycle
statement: The water cycle describes water moving among atmosphere, surface, subsurface, ice, and living systems through processes including evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, runoff, and storage.
limitations: Fluxes and storage times vary greatly by location, season, climate, and human intervention.

title: Weather and climate
statement: Weather describes atmospheric conditions over relatively short times and local scales, while climate describes statistical patterns and variability of weather over longer periods and broader contexts.
limitations: The boundary is conceptual rather than one universal time cutoff, and climate includes variability as well as averages.

title: Cell theory
statement: Cell theory treats cells as the basic structural and functional units of living organisms and holds that new cells arise from existing cells through biological division.
limitations: Viruses and other acellular biological entities require separate treatment and do not invalidate the cellular organization of organisms.

title: DNA and inherited information
statement: In cellular organisms, DNA stores heritable sequence information that can be replicated and expressed through regulated molecular processes involving RNA and proteins.
limitations: Phenotype is not determined by DNA sequence alone; regulation, development, environment, and stochastic effects also matter.

title: Evolution by natural selection
statement: When heritable variants differ in survival or reproductive success in a given environment, their frequencies can change across generations through natural selection.
limitations: Natural selection is one evolutionary process among mutation, migration, recombination, and genetic drift; it has no predetermined goal.

title: Incidence and prevalence
statement: Incidence measures new events arising in a population over a specified period, while prevalence measures existing cases or states in a population at a specified time or over a specified interval.
limitations: Numerators, denominators, time windows, case definitions, and sampling methods must be specified for valid comparison.

title: Vaccination and immune memory
statement: Vaccination exposes the immune system to selected antigens or antigen instructions so that adaptive immune responses can develop memory before later exposure to the targeted pathogen.
limitations: Effectiveness, duration, contraindications, and schedules vary by vaccine and population; this claim is not individual medical advice.

title: Population evidence and individual care
statement: Population-level clinical evidence informs care but does not by itself establish a diagnosis or treatment choice for a particular person; clinical context and qualified judgment remain necessary.
limitations: This safety boundary does not replace emergency guidance or consultation with a licensed clinician.

title: Crop rotation
statement: Crop rotation changes the crop grown on a field over time and can be designed to influence nutrient use, pest and disease cycles, soil structure, and production risk.
limitations: Benefits depend on local soils, climate, crop sequence, management, and economic constraints.

title: Soil as a coupled system
statement: Agricultural soil is a coupled physical, chemical, and biological system in which mineral particles, organic matter, water, air, and organisms jointly affect plant growth and nutrient cycling.
limitations: No single indicator completely describes soil function across all crops, climates, and management goals.

title: One Health connection
statement: Human, animal, plant, and environmental health are interconnected, so surveillance and prevention of some diseases benefit from coordinated work across medical, veterinary, ecological, and agricultural fields.
limitations: Coordination does not erase the distinct methods, authorities, and evidence standards of each participating field.
